description: A replica-1 proposal establishes nonzero value ballot; a generated Prepare asks its owner to report retained history. Compare producer vbal sampled synchronously after reply emission to the matching actual decoded value ballot.

harness.description: TestAssurancePrepareValueBallot; unchanged handlers and codecs, byte-stream links and deterministic dispatch, no workers or resources requiring cleanup.
semantic_changes: Bounded constructor-equivalent replicas omit network and execution goroutine startup.
Real SendMsg/Marshal and New/Unmarshal operate over per-link byte buffers.
A decoded PreAcceptReply is held pending while a later Prepare on a different message-type channel is dispatched.
Recovery entry is invoked for a known unresolved slot instead of waiting for the scanner timer.

legality.derivation: Reuse only constructor and wire helpers after checking this history: N=3,F=1, original owner replica 1 proposes through handlePropose, establishing vbal=1. Replica 2 receives its actual PreAccept and has a known uncommitted slot covered by crtInstance, permitting the recovery entry. The original PreAcceptReply is decoded first on link 2->1 but retained without handler dispatch. Then an actual startRecoveryForInstance emits Prepare ballot 5; owner 1 handles it before the earlier PreAcceptReply dispatch. This is legal: S_receive decodes before asynchronous per-message channel enqueue and S_dispatch selects separate channels without global FIFO. No reply is fabricated or repeated. All delivered messages are emitted by target handlers and actual codecs. After handlePrepare returns, the same single-owner local vbal copied by that handler is recorded while its serialized reply is queued. Unmarshal decodes that reply into New-produced storage; correlation checks enforce acceptor, instance and request ballot. No recovery reply consumer is invoked and no expected value is written into protocol state.
legality.applicability: Bounded single-thread handler history with explicit per-message dispatch substitution, real codecs, non-durable constructor-equivalent state and small arrays. Recovery timer delay is not measured and no timing property is checked.
unresolved: No end-to-end TCP or recovery quorum decision is executed.
alternatives: If the earlier PreAcceptReply were dispatched first the owner might commit; that is another allowed schedule and not required by the observed transport boundary.

grounding.derivation: handlePrepare explicitly copies local inst.vbal into the reply separate from the promise ballot. The registered Serializable interface and sender/receiver call chain transfer that object; handlePrepareReply uses VBallot to rank retained values. Therefore successful reply transport owes equality of this semantic field with the producer local value ballot for the same report. This is a local preservation duty from actual producer and consumer, not an assumed protocol theorem or arbitrary serialization of unused state.
grounding.applicability: An implementation-produced PrepareReply is serialized through SendMsg and decoded into the registered fresh message type; compare the local value ballot copied by handlePrepare with the corresponding decoded report.
unresolved: Global recovery consequence is not claimed.
alternatives: Other fields and local coordinator history can remain correct despite this field loss.

observable_properties.description: The value ballot read from the decoded reply equals the producer field that handlePrepare copied into the sent report. Identity uses acceptor/origin/instance/recipient and the same fixed Prepare request ballot, never the compared vbal.

uncertainties: One nonzero original-owner value ballot is exercised.
No later recovery decision or application effect is claimed.
